subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Caral: The Americas' Oldest City
description: A 60-second lesson on Caral: The Americas' Oldest City.

hook.text: A city in Peru was thriving at the same time as the Egyptian pyramids. It had no pottery, no weapons, and no war.

buildup.text: Caral was built around 2600 BCE, making it the oldest known city in the Americas by a wide margin.

discovery.text: It has six large platform mounds, sunken plazas, and a residential area — but zero evidence of warfare.

twist.text: Archaeologists found quipus — knotted string records — which were thought to have been invented 3,000 years later by.

climax.text: Caral challenges the idea that civilization requires war. This society built monuments on trade, not conquest.

punchline.text: The oldest American city had pyramids but no army. Peace was its foundation.

quiz.question: What makes Caral unusual compared to other early civilizations?
options: It was built entirely underground to avoid detection
There is zero evidence of warfare — it appears to have been a peaceful society
It was exclusively a religious site with no permanent residents
